detail_facts: All 160 frames · 0–33.80 h; 20 px strip; identical BF translation, tissue masks and shared color limits.
Fig. 1d “0 min” matches the 18.07 h video overlay; start ≈ (150.7, 407.1) video pixels, direction −71.96°.
100 µm = 111 video pixels; each line has its own distance origin, not matched cells.
The new line intersects tissue in 142/160 frames, first at 3.83 h; tissue/FOV gaps stay gray and are not zero-filled.
detail_steps: Register Fig. 1d to Video 2 using image features: 142 reference-frame inliers, median residual 0.31 video pixels, cross-checked against four other time thumbnails. Arrow endpoints are approximate readings of the drawing.

Sample from the illustrated start along its arrow. The full author ROI trajectory is unavailable, so both versions use the current BF translation rule; early origins outside tissue are not moved onto bright regions.

Use original video display values, a 20 px strip and common tissue/FOV validity rules. Allow a missing leading segment and retain the longest continuous valid tissue interval. Recomputing the current version with this rule reproduces its matrix exactly.

The main pair adds no smoothing and shares one min–max color scale over both complete matrices. A separate pair applies the same spatial Gaussian σ=9.66 µm. The current center remains the fit to six early wavefront frames; its audit view is retained.
datasets.detail_limit: This reconstructs the illustrated line, not an author-deposited exact ROI or a verified biological source. Continuing both lines by BF translation is a shared assumption, without deformation correction or cell tracking. Video overlay times are retained rather than recalibrated from inset minute labels; early missing samples do not imply absent expression. Video display values are not raw fluorescence counts.
